digest.headline: US inflation reached 3.8% as the Nasdaq entered a correction and the DAX surged over two percent.

lede.b: US inflation hit 3.8%, which is the rate at which everyday prices rise across the economy. This figure makes traders wonder if the central bank, which is the institution that sets borrowing costs, will alter interest rates at its next meeting. At the same time, the Nasdaq index suffered its worst November since 2008 and entered a correction, which means a drop of 10% or more from recent peaks. Meanwhile, a technical glitch stalled options trading on the CME exchange for 10 minutes at the opening bell. US inflation reached 3.8% and the Nasdaq entered a correction.
lede.i: US inflation printed at 3.8%, altering expectations for the central bank's upcoming December rate decision. Simultaneously, the Nasdaq entered a correction after enduring its worst November since 2008. Technical infrastructure stumbled as a trading glitch halted E-mini S&P 500 options for 10 minutes at the CME opening bell. US inflation reached 3.8% and Nasdaq 100 futures rebounded alongside European equities.
lede.a: US inflation printed at 3.8%, re-pricing December Federal Reserve rate probabilities and driving the Nasdaq into a correction after its worst November since 2008. Market plumbing failed concurrently when an opening-bell glitch at the CME halted E-mini S&P 500 options for 10 minutes. Nasdaq 100 futures subsequently rebounded alongside European tech equities following five days of extreme volatility. US inflation reached 3.8%.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: US tech sell-off, inflation data, and trading glitches

stories.t: Nasdaq Records Sharp Losses While Futures Rebound
stories.b: The Nasdaq index tracks many technology companies. It just had its worst November since 2008. The index is now in a correction phase. Futures contracts, which are agreements to buy assets later at set prices, rose recently.
stories.i: The Nasdaq entered a correction after enduring its worst November since 2008. Meanwhile, Nasdaq 100 futures climbed alongside European tech equities. This movement follows a volatile five-day stretch for the index not seen since April 2025.
stories.a: The Nasdaq 100 experienced its highest volatility five-day window since April 2025 during a wider correction. Futures recovered alongside European peers on spillover support from regional market rebounds. The index continues to trade through its most severe November drawdown since 2008.

stories.t: US Inflation Reaches 3.8% As Market Glitch Hits Options
stories.b: Consumer inflation hit 3.8% in the United States. Inflation is the rate at which prices rise over time. Traders now wonder if the central bank will raise interest rates in December. Separately, a technical glitch paused E-mini S&P 500 options for roughly 10 minutes at the market open on the CME exchange.
stories.i: US inflation reached 3.8%, prompting speculation over whether the central bank will alter interest rates at its December meeting. Market plumbing also suffered disruptions when a technical glitch stalled E-mini S&P 500 options for roughly 10 minutes at the opening bell on the CME.
stories.a: Headline inflation printed at 3.8%, recalibrating market expectations for the central bank's upcoming December rate decision. Operational resilience faced a test when a CME glitch halted E-mini S&P 500 options trading for approximately 10 minutes during the opening sequence.

politics.b: Government authorities track inflation data to manage the economy. Central bank officials decide on interest rates. Public regulators oversee financial exchanges.
politics.i: Federal authorities monitor price indexes to gauge economic health. Central bank policymakers weigh rate adjustments against macroeconomic data. Market regulators oversee exchange infrastructure following technical outages.
politics.a: Monetary authorities parse price metrics to calibrate policy paths. Central bank officials face decisions regarding December tightening. Exchange operators manage system redundancy following automated trading halts.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: Bank tax warnings and corporate departures in the UK

stories.t: Bank of England warns over tax hikes and AI debt risks
stories.b: The head of the Bank of England warned that banks might push a £1.5bn tax increase onto everyday customers. Central banks are official institutions that manage a country's money supply and interest rates. The same central bank also warned that borrowing money to fund artificial intelligence projects creates rising financial risks. This means taking on debt for new technology could destabilise the financial system if projects fail.
stories.i: The Bank of England cautioned that lenders could pass a £1.5bn tax hike directly onto consumers. Meanwhile, the central institution highlighted escalating financial vulnerabilities stemming from AI borrowing. Lenders extending credit for artificial intelligence ventures are building up hidden exposures. These leveraged bets could amplify systemic shocks if technology valuations correct.
stories.a: The Bank of England flagged potential consumer pass-through of a £1.5bn tax burden by domestic lenders. Concurrently, the institution singled out AI-driven credit creation as a vector for systemic fragility. Second-order feedback loops from tech-sector leverage could impair bank balance sheets if collateral values deteriorate. The implied risk metric suggests underwriting standards are lagging behind rapid capital deployment in artificial intelligence.

stories.t: Britain faces blue-chip departures and student enrollment drops
stories.b: Major British companies, known as blue chips, keep leaving the country to list their shares elsewhere. Shares are tiny slices of ownership in a company that people buy and sell on a stock market. At the same time, the government received warnings that falling numbers of international students are damaging both universities and the wider economy.
stories.i: Major British blue-chip corporations continue to exit domestic stock markets for foreign venues. Simultaneously, the government received warnings that declining international student enrollment is actively harming universities and the broader economy.
stories.a: UK equity capital markets face persistent headwinds as prime blue-chip issuers execute primary listings abroad. Concurrently, secular declines in international student matriculation threaten institutional revenues across the higher education sector, compounding macroeconomic drag.

politics.b: The government received direct warnings that declining international student numbers are hurting the economy and universities.
politics.i: Ministers faced official warnings regarding the economic damage caused by falling international student numbers.
politics.a: policymakers absorbed empirical warnings linking visa and immigration dynamics in higher education directly to structural economic degradation.

timeline: Bank of England warns of financial risks tied to AI borrowing.
Bank of England chief warns banks may pass a £1.5bn tax hike to customers.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German stocks rally as consumer sentiment and tech recover

stories.t: DAX Surges Over Two Percent
stories.b: Stocks are shares of ownership in a company that people buy and sell. The DAX is a major stock index, which is a group representing the biggest companies in Germany. This German stock index jumped 2.08% to close at 25,215.52 points. Technology and automotive companies led this strong market rebound.
stories.i: Equities advanced sharply as the DAX gained 2.08% to finish the session at 25,215.52 points. Technology and auto shares recovered ground after recent selling pressure. Renewed technical buying interest propelled the index higher during thin trading conditions.
stories.a: The blue-chip DAX rallied 2.08% to close at 25,215.52 points, driven by a rebound in tech and auto components. Technical buying interest dominated a session characterized by thinner liquidity as US markets closed for Thanksgiving. Momentum indicators shifted positive as the index pushed toward immediate resistance levels.

stories.t: Consumer Sentiment Ticks Up Alongside Tariff Relief
stories.b: Consumer sentiment measures how optimistic shoppers feel about the economy. The forecast for German consumer sentiment in December ticked higher. Meanwhile, new US tariff proposals eased worries for international trade. European stocks rallied across the board following these updates.
stories.i: German consumer sentiment forecasts for December ticked up slightly to support sentiment. European equities drew additional strength as US tariff proposals eased earlier market concerns. Technology shares recovered across regional indices including the DAX, CAC, and FTSE 100.
stories.a: December consumer sentiment forecasts ticked higher, lending fundamental support to the domestic consumer outlook. Regional equities found macro relief as US tariff proposals alleviated severe trade anxiety. Technology shares across European benchmarks recovered concurrently.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Tokyo inflation data, JERA data centre talks, and tobacco bid

stories.t: Tokyo Inflation Preview Ahead of Central Bank Decision
stories.b: Tokyo core inflation is forecast to jump to 3%. Inflation means prices are going up over time. This report arrives three weeks before a Bank of Japan decision. The Yen is trading under 160.00 against the US dollar. A central bank hawk is flagging further monetary tightening.
stories.i: Tokyo core inflation is forecast to jump to 3%. This release precedes the Bank of Japan decision by three weeks, with the Yen trading under 160.00 against the US dollar. A central bank hawk is flagging further monetary tightening. Scotiabank notes the upcoming consumer price index release.
stories.a: Tokyo core inflation is projected to print at 3% three weeks prior to the Bank of Japan policy meeting. The spot rate for the Yen remains under 160.00 against the US dollar. A Bank of Japan hawk has signaled potential policy tightening, putting focus on the upcoming consumer price index print.

stories.t: JERA Enters Talks With Anthropic and Meta
stories.b: Japan's JERA is entering talks with Anthropic and Meta. The goal is to build data centres near power plants. Nikkei reports this development. JERA aims to position the new facilities close to energy sources.
stories.i: Japan's JERA is entering talks with Anthropic and Meta. Nikkei reports that the companies plan to build data centres near power plants. JERA aims to co-locate these digital infrastructure projects with its power generation sites.
stories.a: Japan's JERA has initiated discussions with Anthropic and Meta regarding the construction of data centres. According to Nikkei reports, the infrastructure is intended to be built in close proximity to power plants. JERA seeks to secure direct power access for these heavy energy-consuming facilities.

stories.t: Altria Explores Imperial Bid With Possible Japan Tobacco Tie-Up
stories.b: Marlboro maker Altria is exploring a bid for Imperial. It is possibly doing this with Japan Tobacco. Nikkei Asia reports the tobacco companies are reviewing options. Altria is looking at the potential acquisition structure.
stories.i: Altria is exploring an Imperial bid, potentially partnering with Japan Tobacco. Nikkei Asia reports that the Marlboro maker is examining the transaction structure. Japan Tobacco could join the pursuit of Imperial Brands.
stories.a: Altria is exploring a prospective bid for Imperial, evaluating a joint approach with Japan Tobacco. Nikkei Asia reports that the Marlboro manufacturer is weighing transaction structures for the asset. Japan Tobacco's potential involvement remains under consideration.

China.label: China
China.sub: Yuan moves, corporate bond extensions and iron ore demand

stories.t: Euro Drops Against Yuan as Iron Ore Prices Rise
stories.b: The euro is heading for its biggest drop against the Chinese yuan in 20 years. Iron ore prices rose because Chinese mills expect to restock for the winter. Iron ore is a raw material used to make steel.
stories.i: The euro is on track for its steepest annual decline against the yuan in two decades. Iron ore prices climbed as Chinese steel mills prepared for seasonal winter restocking.
stories.a: The euro headed toward its sharpest yearly depreciation against the yuan in 20 years. Iron ore futures appreciated as market participants anticipated winter inventory restocking across Chinese steel mills.

stories.t: Vanke Seeks Bond Extension and LSEG Sells Yuan Debt
stories.b: Vanke is asking for a second extension on a 1.2 billion yuan bond. A bond is a loan where an investor lends money to a company. The London Stock Exchange Group raised $300 million by selling yuan bonds to diversify its debt.
stories.i: Vanke requested a second extension on a 1.2 billion yuan gilt equivalent. The London Stock Exchange Group raised $300 million through yuan-denominated debt issuance as part of a diversification strategy.
stories.a: Vanke sought a secondary maturity extension on a 1.2 billion yuan corporate note. The London Stock Exchange Group priced a $300 million equivalent yuan bond offering to execute a debt diversification initiative.

politics.b: Kevin Rudd discussed Xi Jinping, the Chinese economy, and how to deter a war over Taiwan.
politics.i: Kevin Rudd evaluated Xi Jinping, the trajectory of the Chinese economy, and deterrence strategies regarding a Taiwan conflict.
politics.a: Kevin Rudd analyzed the leadership of Xi Jinping, structural economic conditions in China, and deterrence mechanisms concerning a potential Taiwan conflict.

India.label: India
India.sub: Stock gains, RBI repo auction, and rupee movements

stories.t: Stock Markets and JP Morgan Nifty Target
stories.src: Kotak Neo · The Times of India · LinkedIn
stories.b: The Sensex index went up by nearly 400 points, and the Nifty index got close to 26,600. An index is a way to track the value of a group of companies. The Sensex also touched a 10-month high. JP Morgan predicted the Nifty will reach 29,000 by the end of 2027.
stories.i: The Sensex climbed close to 400 points while the Nifty approached 26,600, pushing the Sensex near a 10-month high. JP Morgan forecasted that the Nifty will hit 29,000 by the end of 2027. The financial institution also projected three more rate hikes from the central bank.
stories.a: Equities advanced as the Sensex gained nearly 400 points and the Nifty neared 26,600, touching a 10-month high. JP Morgan projected the Nifty will reach 29,000 by the end of 2027 alongside a trajectory of three additional monetary tightening steps. Market participants evaluated these equity gains against forward rate expectations.

stories.t: Reserve Bank of India Variable Rate Repo Auction
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India decided to hold a Variable Rate Repo auction on November 27, 2026. This auction lets banks borrow money from the central bank. The Reserve Bank will offer 75,000 crore rupees for three days. Banks will return the funds on November 30, 2026.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India announced a Variable Rate Repo auction for November 27, 2026, to manage near-term liquidity. The central bank will auction 75,000 crore rupees with a three-day tenor. Counterparties can bid in the window from 09:30 AM to 10:00 AM, with a reversal date set for November 30, 2026.
stories.a: Liquidity management operations by the Reserve Bank of India comprise a 75,000 crore rupee Variable Rate Repo auction scheduled for November 27, 2026. The three-day facility operates via a morning bidding window from 09:30 AM to 10:00 AM. Settlement and reversal occur on November 30, 2026.

stories.t: Rupee Moves and Analyst Warnings
stories.b: The rupee fell by 18 paise to 92.38 against the US dollar. Some analysts warned the central bank should avoid a jumbo interest rate hike in December. They said a big rate hike could cause money to leave the country and make the rupee unstable.
stories.i: The rupee declined 18 paise to trade at 92.38 against the US dollar. Analysts cautioned that the central bank should avoid a jumbo rate hike in December. Such a move could trigger capital outflows and introduce currency instability.
stories.a: Spot transactions placed the rupee 18 paise lower at 92.38 against the US dollar. Commentary warned against a jumbo rate hike in December to mitigate potential capital outflows and subsequent foreign exchange volatility. Market participants weighed these currency pressures against macroeconomic fundamentals.

politics.i: The Supreme Court redrew food labels. Tata Trusts initiated legal action against Chandra.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Stocks surge and currency gains following fiscal package and data

stories.t: Ibovespa Surges and Currency Strengthens
stories.b: Brazil's main stock market index, called the Ibovespa, jumped by 6% in one day. The value of the US dollar fell against the Brazilian real for the fourth straight session. Lower-than-expected inflation and a new fiscal package drove these market moves. The dollar dropped by almost 2% against the real following the package approval.
stories.i: The Ibovespa surged 6% as a possible Trabuco appointment to the Finance Ministry lifted sentiment. Softer inflation prints combined with the approval of Brazil's fiscal package to drive the US dollar down against the real for the fourth consecutive session. Shorter-term selling also pushed the euro down by 1.5% against the real.
stories.a: Equities rallied aggressively with the Ibovespa advancing 6% alongside a fourth consecutive daily decline for the US dollar against the real. Market participants priced in fiscal optimism stemming from the legislative approval of the fiscal package and potential cabinet appointments. Lower inflation prints compounded the currency appreciation and broader risk-on sentiment across local asset classes.

stories.t: Petrobras Approves Plan and Faces Scrutiny
stories.src: Prop News Time · TradingView · CPG Click Oil and Gas
stories.b: State-controlled oil company Petrobras approved a five-year plan worth $122 billion and announced an extra dividend of $2.6 billion. The company also halted oil production at the FPSO P-77 platform due to signs of fire. Petrobras faces an ethics complaint regarding its alleged efforts to influence energy regulators over natural gas tariffs for the years 2026 to 2030. Furthermore, the firm plans to remove 27 offshore platforms by 2031 at a cost of $11.2 billion.
stories.i: Petrobras approved a USD 122 billion five-year plan alongside a USD 2.6 billion extra dividend. Operations hit a snag as the company halted oil production at FPSO P-77 due to signs of fire. Regulatory friction emerged as Petrobras faced an ethics complaint over alleged influence on ANP during the 2026 to 2030 natural gas tariff review. Meanwhile, the firm scheduled the removal of 27 offshore platforms by 2031 for USD 11.2 billion and listed platforms P-19 and P-26 for online auction.
stories.a: Capital allocation updates feature a USD 122 billion five-year plan and a USD 2.6 billion extra dividend authorization by Petrobras. Operational disruptions materialized via an emergency production halt at FPSO P-77 following fire indicators. Governance challenges intensified as the company faced an ethics complaint concerning alleged interference with ANP during the 2026-2030 natural gas transportation tariff review. Decommissioning liabilities expanded as management outlined plans to remove 27 offshore platforms by 2031 at an estimated cost of USD 11.2 billion.

politics.b: Government officials worked on a new fiscal package and budget reforms. Lawmakers debated economic policies and potential cabinet positions. These actions influenced the value of the national currency against foreign money.
politics.i: Fiscal package approvals and economic cabinet announcements drove currency fluctuations. The administration advanced legislative reforms that improved market confidence in public accounts. Speculation regarding high-profile ministry appointments also circulated among market participants.
politics.a: Fiscal consolidation measures advanced through legislative approval channels, triggering broad-based adjustments in foreign exchange risk premiums. Cabinet appointment rumors regarding the Finance Ministry intersected with fiscal policy announcements to shape sovereign risk pricing. Market sentiment reacted directly to the fiscal framework's progression through policy channels.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Refinery attack and foreign bank confidence

stories.t: Houthi Projectile Hits Jazan Refinery
stories.b: An oil refinery is a factory that turns crude oil into useful fuels like petrol. A projectile attack hit the Jazan refinery belonging to Saudi Aramco on 26 November 2026. The Saudi Energy Ministry confirmed that one worker from Nepal died in the blast. The strike forced the company to shut down some operational units at the facility.
stories.i: A projectile strike hit Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery on 26 November 2026, according to the Saudi Energy Ministry. The attack killed one Nepalese worker and forced the suspension of select processing units. The Saudi-led coalition attributed the assault to Houthi forces.
stories.a: A Houthi projectile targeted Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery on 26 November 2026, resulting in a fatality and the partial curtailment of processing capacity. The Saudi-led coalition confirmed the attribution, while the Energy Ministry verified the death of a Nepalese national and the localized operational shutdown.

stories.t: Barclays Affirms Saudi Economic Outlook
stories.b: Barclays is a large global bank that provides financial services around the world. The bank stated its strong belief in the Saudi economy on 26 November 2026. Barclays also expressed its desire to participate in the nation's ongoing economic transformation plans.
stories.i: Barclays reiterated its positive outlook on the Saudi economy on 26 November 2026. The institution also signaled its intention to secure a role in the country's economic transformation initiatives.
stories.a: Barclays reaffirmed its macro confidence in the Saudi economy on 26 November 2026. Management concurrently articulated an ambition to participate in the kingdom's structural economic transformation program.

politics.b: South Korea and Saudi Arabia agreed to work more closely together on oil stockpiling on 26 November 2026. This agreement comes during discussions over South Korea's petrochemical restructuring.
politics.i: South Korea and Saudi Arabia formalized closer ties on oil stockpiling on 26 November 2026. The agreement coincides with discussions regarding Seoul's domestic petrochemical restructuring efforts.
politics.a: South Korea and Saudi Arabia established closer bilateral cooperation in oil stockpiling on 26 November 2026. The agreement runs parallel to ongoing industry deliberations surrounding Seoul's petrochemical restructuring agenda.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira rate movements, central bank currency trial, and asset rules

stories.t: Naira Exchange Rates and Currency Dispute
stories.src: MSME Africa · New African Magazine · Premium Times Nigeria
stories.b: The local currency dropped to ₦1,455 per dollar as buyers demanded more foreign money. Former president Olusegun Obasanjo stated that currency drops left the country impoverished. Meanwhile, a witness told a court that former central bank governor Godwin Emefiele executed a colour swap instead of an approved redesign.
stories.i: The naira fell to ₦1,455 against the dollar amid rising greenback demand and declining reserves. Former leader Olusegun Obasanjo argued that inflation-related currency drops impoverished the nation. Testimony in court revealed that former central bank governor Godwin Emefiele implemented a colour swap that deviated from presidential approval.
stories.a: Spot rates depreciated to ₦1,455 per dollar as dollar demand accelerated and external reserves contracted. Former head of state Olusegun Obasanjo criticized historical parity adjustments for impoverishing the state. Judicial proceedings disclosed that former governor Godwin Emefiele executed an unauthorized colour swap instead of the sanctioned redesign.

stories.t: New Virtual Asset Rules Issued
stories.b: The Central Bank of Nigeria published new rules for non-security virtual assets. These digital items now fall under specific government oversight. Authorities released the framework to control their operation.
stories.i: The Central Bank of Nigeria introduced operating regulations for non-security virtual assets. Digital token platforms must now comply with these official guidelines. The central bank published the framework to govern non-security crypto operations.
stories.a: The Central Bank of Nigeria promulgated regulatory frameworks for non-security virtual assets. Compliance parameters now bind digital asset operators under official guidelines. The central bank instituted these controls to monitor non-security crypto activities.

politics.b: A witness testified in court regarding the actions of former central bank governor Godwin Emefiele. Prosecutors examined how redesigned currency differed from presidential orders. Meanwhile, fact-checkers debunked a false online link claiming a senator was giving away cash.
politics.i: Court proceedings investigated former central bank governor Godwin Emefiele over currency redesign discrepancies. Witnesses detailed how the executed notes departed from the approval granted by former president Muhammadu Buhari. Separate reports debunked social media links falsely claiming cash empowerment handouts from Senator Yayi.
politics.a: Judicial hearings scrutinized former governor Godwin Emefiele regarding procedural deviations in the currency redesign from presidential mandates. Witnesses confirmed the executed swap diverged from the terms authorized by former president Muhammadu Buhari. Independent investigations simultaneously refuted fraudulent digital campaigns falsely attributing cash distributions to Senator Yayi.

timeline: Witnesses testified in court that Godwin Emefiele's currency redesign differed from presidential approval.
The Central Bank of Nigeria issued operational rules for non-security virtual assets.

stories.b: Macquarie Bank lost its chief executive officer and group chief operating officer to retirement. These departures happened as the firm shifts toward digital operations. The two leaders stepped down from their posts. Their exits were announced on 26 November 2026.
stories.i: Macquarie Bank announced the retirement of its bank CEO and group COO. The departures coincide with a strategic pivot toward digital operations within the firm. Both top executives are stepping down from their respective roles. The bank confirmed the changes on 26 November 2026.
stories.a: Macquarie Bank announced the simultaneous retirement of its bank CEO and group COO amid an organizational pivot toward digital infrastructure. The executive departures mark a generational shift in leadership for the financial institution as operational models evolve. Both executives officially vacate their posts following the announcement on 26 November 2026.

stories.t: Australian Shares Eye Positive Open
stories.b: Australian shares were set to rise at the start of trading. Oil prices jumped higher globally. Global stocks also rallied while Wall Street remained shut. The Australian dollar edged higher against major currencies.
stories.i: The ASX prepared for modest gains following a jump in global oil prices. International equities rallied while Wall Street remained closed. Meanwhile, the Australian dollar edged up but faced resistance near 0.6700 due to US Federal Reserve rate hike bets.
stories.a: The ASX futures pointed to a higher open following overnight oil gains and a broad rally in international equities during a US market closure. The Australian dollar ticked up but remained capped below the 0.6700 threshold as market participants priced in persistent Federal Reserve tightening expectations.
